description: We are ASTRAVYNE, a team of student innovators passionate about AI, space technology, and solving real-world challenges. Our mission is to transform NASA Earth observation data into smart, practical solutions for climate-resilient farming. We bring skills in software development, AI, and engineering, and welcome teammates with expertise in agriculture, GIS, satellite data, and UI/UX. Together, we aim to empower farmers through innovation and sustainable technology.
summary:
ASTRAVYNE — Spatial Intelligence for Climate-Resilient Agriculture

ASTRAVYNE is a Spatial Intelligence-powered agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the theme "Resilient Crop Rotation Using NASA Data." Our mission is to transform NASA Earth observations into actionable insights that help farmers make sustainable, climate-resilient decisions.

Agriculture faces growing challenges from unpredictable rainfall, rising temperatures, soil degradation, and water scarcity. ASTRAVYNE addresses these issues by combining satellite observations, agricultural knowledge, and location-specific environmental information.

Our platform integrates NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM, Landsat, MODIS, and ECOSTRESS datasets to analyze rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation health, and environmental stress. Our initial prototype focuses on Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.

At its core, ASTRAVYNE features a Spatial Intelligence Engine designed to assess crop suitability, generate potential crop rotation sequences, and evaluate alternatives based on water efficiency, soil health, climate resilience, and agricultural feasibility.

Through an interactive geographical interface, farmers can explore environmental conditions, compare crop rotations, and understand the reasoning behind recommendations.

ASTRAVYNE aims to bridge NASA Earth science and sustainable agriculture, helping farmers understand what to grow, where, when, and why.
details:
ASTRAVYNE — Project Details

ASTRAVYNE is a Spatial Intelligence-based agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of building climate-resilient crop rotation strategies using NASA Earth observation data.

Problem Statement:
Farmers face unpredictable rainfall, rising temperatures, soil degradation, and water scarcity. Conventional crop planning often lacks access to location-specific environmental intelligence, making it difficult to select sustainable crop rotations.

Our Solution:
ASTRAVYNE combines NASA satellite observations, agricultural knowledge, and farmer-specific information to analyze environmental conditions and recommend suitable crop rotation strategies.

Technology and Data Sources:
The platform integrates NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM, Landsat, MODIS, and ECOSTRESS datasets to study rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation health, and environmental stress.

Core Architecture:
Our Spatial Intelligence Engine is designed to perform environmental profiling, crop suitability analysis, rotation generation, historical climate stress testing, and multi-criteria evaluation. It compares crop rotations based on water efficiency, soil health, climate resilience, and agricultural feasibility.

Key Features:

  • Interactive geographical exploration and environmental visualization.
  • Location-specific crop suitability assessment.
  • Climate-resilient crop rotation recommendations.
  • Historical environmental analysis and risk evaluation.
  • Explainable recommendations supported by scientific evidence.

Prototype and Impact:
Our initial prototype focuses on Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, with an architecture designed for future geographical expansion.

ASTRAVYNE aims to bridge NASA Earth science and practical agriculture, enabling farmers to understand what to grow, when to grow it, and why certain crop rotations are more suitable for their land.

Our ultimate goal is to make satellite-powered agricultural intelligence accessible, explainable, and useful for sustainable farming.
